title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 154 (Liability of bailee making unauthorised use of goods bailed)

content.overview: Section 154 provides that if the bailee makes any use of the goods bailed which is not according to the conditions of the bailment, he is liable to make compensation to the bailor for any damage arising to the goods from or during such use of them. Two statutory illustrations confirm liability even where care is taken but the use is unauthorised.
content.glance: Bailee who makes unauthorised use of the goods is liable to compensate the bailor for damage arising from or during that use.
content.study: If the bailee makes any use of the goods bailed which is not according to the conditions of the bailment, he is liable to make compensation to the bailor for any damage arising to the goods from or during such use of them. Illustrations: (a) horse lent for own riding only, allowed to another who rides carefully but horse is injured — bailee liable; (b) horse hired to march to one place, taken to another, injured despite care — bailee liable. Current-law framing: liability attaches to the unauthorised use itself, even if ordinary care is taken during that use.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: If the bailee makes any use of the goods bailed which is not according to the conditions of the bailment, he is liable to make compensation to the bailor for any damage arising to the goods from or during such use of them.

sections.heading: Statutory illustrations
sections.body: (a) A lends a horse to B for his own riding only. B allows C, a member of his family, to ride the horse. C rides with care, but the horse accidentally falls and is injured. B is liable to make compensation to A for the injury done to the horse. (b) A hires a horse in Calcutta from B expressly to march to Banaras. A rides with due care but marches to Cuttack instead. The horse accidentally falls and is injured. A is liable to make compensation to B for the injury to the horse.

examples.title: Unauthorised rider
examples.body: Horse lent only for the bailee’s own riding is allowed to another; injury occurs despite care. Bailee is liable under Section 154.

examples.title: Deviation from agreed route
examples.body: Horse hired for a journey to one place is taken to another; injury occurs despite care. Bailee is liable under Section 154.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee uses the goods contrary to the conditions but takes care. Goods are damaged. Is he liable?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 154 makes the bailee liable for damage arising from or during the unauthorised use, even if care is taken.

illustrations: Section 154 Illustration (a): unauthorised rider, careful riding, injury — bailee liable.
Section 154 Illustration (b): deviation from agreed destination, careful riding, injury — bailee liable.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 154 provides that if the bailee makes any use of the goods bailed which is not according to the conditions of the bailment, he is liable to make compensation to the bailor for any damage arising to the goods from or during such use of them. The illustrations confirm that liability arises even where the unauthorised user or the bailee rides with care and the injury is accidental. This is complementary to the termination right under Section 153.
examples: Unauthorised rider or deviation from agreed route — liability for resulting injury.
distinctions: Section 154 addresses compensation for damage from unauthorised use; Section 153 addresses the option to terminate the bailment.

keyTakeaways: Unauthorised use creates liability for damage from or during that use.
Care during the unauthorised use does not avoid liability.
